# Frozen revision 9 linked harmonic compression

The oracle calls unchanged `render_room.glue` for deterministic synthetic inputs. Realistic cases execute unchanged `session_render.render_song` with the original 3,711,911-frame allocation and the accepted 63-event prefix, then capture the harmonic output immediately after focus gains/glue and before room. They retain only the first 416,000 frames. The original duration, reflection boundary, and rack fades are preserved; no shortened allocation is used for the harmonic capture. The alternate piano focus changes only the focus setting, not the injected performance.

Every input frame contains guitar left/right, piano left/right, bass left/right, drums left/right, and duck. Every output frame contains compressed tonal left/right, delayed bass left/right, delayed drums left/right, and duck. Candidates contain logical output after removing exactly 399 startup frames. For synthetic cases, process all `input_frames`, drain 399 physical frames, then retain exactly `frames` logical outputs. For realistic cases, declare the full original `input_frames`, process `frames + 399`, retain `frames` logical outputs, and do not prematurely drain the partial rack.

Eleven complete short cases cover lengths 1, 2, 3, 17, 399, 400, 401, 799, 800, 801, and 4,097. They contain asymmetric endpoint/center impulses and alternating focus settings; the 800/801 cases place their middle impulses at frames 399/400. Both 48,000-frame dynamics cases share exact dyadic Float32 inputs spanning below-threshold levels, the soft knee, linear reduction, the 5 dB cap, opposite polarity, one-sided stereo, instrument cancellation, release/recovery, and a nonzero final boundary. Distinct bass/drum/duck patterns independently detect delay errors. Inputs are fixture-authored signals, never generated by native DSP. Empty-stream lifecycle coverage belongs to native tests because original glue does not define an empty reduction minimum.

Acceptance limits are declared before native comparison: maximum error `2e-6` and RMS `2e-7` for synthetic outputs; `1e-5` and `1e-6` for realistic outputs, retaining the existing note-endpoint rounding allowance. The tonal pair is compared separately so pass-through channels cannot dilute its error. Synthetic pass-through fields and every duck field must match exactly after alignment. Finite values, exact byte counts and candidate inventory are mandatory; realistic output must reach exact late silence. The original 800-frame centered detector uses power frames `i-400` through `i+399` with endpoint-repeating reflection. Startup/drain accounting and arbitrary callback partitions are native test requirements.

Small cases retain complete original seven-channel Float32 outputs, with file hashes. Longer cases retain full reference PCM hashes, deterministic sample probes, channel peak/RMS, and maximum gain reduction. CI regenerates every complete compared waveform through the frozen functions; fingerprint agreement alone is not waveform parity. Whole-array reference hashes describe the freezing platform and are reported beside regeneration hashes, since harmless platform floating-point differences can change them. Input and stored expected-file hashes are enforced exactly.

`freeze-glue.py` refuses replacement without explicit `--replace` and never runs in CI. `verify-glue.py --compare .build/tonal-native/glue --evidence .build/tonal-evidence/glue` writes aligned harmonic-only A/B WAVs labeled **unmastered, pre-room**, with hashes, loudness, true-peak estimates, and comparison metrics. They omit room, `.92` dry scaling, final rhythm combination, synthetic air, mastering, and playback. The bass/drum fields are retained for alignment only. No runtime Python or new app assets are introduced; all earlier frozen sources and fixtures remain unchanged.
